# **I. Project Introduction** {#i.-project-introduction}

## **1\. Overview** {#1.-overview}

### **1.1 Project Information** {#1.1-project-information}

* Project name: AI-assisted Emergency Dispatch System with Vision-Language-based Hazard Classification and Severity Scoring   
* Project code: FA26SE242  
* Group name: GFA26SE29  
* Software type: Cross-platform (Mobile application for Android, Web application and Progressive Web App) 

### **1.2 Project Overview** {#1.2-project-overview}

The project designs and develops a closed-loop, real-time emergency coordination and dispatch platform tailored for High-Tech Parks (HTP). The platform connects on-site workers/citizens, the Park Security & Incident Command Center, and internal mobile rescue/patrol units via a shared geolocation-based workflow (GIS).

Through a dedicated mobile client, Citizen can report urgent incidents (Fires and internal Transport Collisions/Accidents) via a One-Touch SOS button with attached scene imagery, as well as submit auxiliary reports on internal traffic bottlenecks. The core differentiator of the system is the integration of a Vision-Language Model (Qwen2.5-VL) to automatically parse incoming media, identify hazard categories (\#Fire, \#Accident, \#Traffic\_Jam), and assign an objective severity rating (Level 0–3 for emergencies). Operating under a Human-in-the-Loop paradigm, the Command Center web dashboard equips dispatch operators with AI-assisted pre-filtering, a prioritized incident queue, real-time fleet tracking, and automated nearest-available or load-aware dispatch matching to accelerate on-scene arrival and optimize road clearance.

## **2\. Project Background** {#2.-project-background}

High-Tech Parks present dense concentrations of manufacturing facilities, warehouses, and thousands of workers, making operational safety risks exceptionally high. Among these risks, workshop fires, electrical short circuits, and internal transport collisions pose immediate threats to human lives and industrial assets. Furthermore, during peak shift transitions, high volumes of commuter vehicles and logistics container trucks frequently trigger severe traffic congestion at security gates and primary arterial corridors, creating roadblocks that severely delay internal emergency responders.

Currently, emergency reporting and response coordination in these parks rely almost entirely on verbal phone calls to the security control room or two-way radio channels. This conventional workflow exhibits multiple vulnerabilities:

Vague scene reporting: Callers under stress frequently provide ambiguous location descriptions (e.g., "near Workshop X" or "behind Gate Y") without visual confirmation of actual scene hazards.

Subjective manual triage: Dispatch operators must estimate incident scale and required response purely from verbal descriptions, leading to misjudged severity levels.

Heuristic and uncoordinated dispatching: Patrol and mini-fire units are typically dispatched based on operator personal familiarity rather than real-time vehicle coordinates, current task loads, and equipment availability.

Lack of operational visibility: Park authorities and on-site workers have no real-time status visibility (ETA, responding team progress) once units are deployed, and routes often collide with unmonitored internal traffic gridlocks.

Recent advancements in Multimodal AI—specifically Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like Qwen2.5-VL— provide an effective technical foundation to bridge this gap. Rather than relying solely on caller verbal accounts, an integrated VLM pipeline can analyze scene media, tag core hazards, detect traffic congestion, and determine severity levels (Levels 0–3).

This project was conceived to address this operational challenge by deploying a practical, human-in-the-loop coordination system. By fusing real-time spatial telemetry, automated VLM hazard classification, and intelligent unit allocation, the platform directly minimizes the critical time window between incident detection, operator verification, and on-scene response within industrial park boundaries.

## **3\. Project Objective** {#3.-project-objective}

The overarching objective of this project is to build and evaluate a real-time, AI-assisted emergency dispatch and coordination platform for High-Tech and Industrial Parks that leverages Qwen2.5-VL to streamline incident verification, prioritize high-risk events, and optimize rescue unit allocation.

Specific project objectives include:

* Citizen/Worker Mobile Application: Develop a responsive mobile client featuring a One-Touch SOS button for emergency reporting (Fires and Accidents) with automatic GPS acquisition and photo/video upload, live ETA/responder tracking, and an auxiliary traffic jam reporting utility.  
* Multimodal AI Evaluation & Pipeline Integration: Integrate and evaluate a Vision-Language Model (Qwen2.5-VL) to classify core hazards (\#Fire, \#Accident), detect internal traffic bottlenecks (\#Traffic\_Jam), and generate standardized severity ratings (Level 0 to Level 3\) from scene media.  
* Command Center Web Dashboard: Engineer an interactive web dashboard for dispatch operators with a WebSocket-driven real-time live map, priority-ranked incident queue, congestion marker overlays, and semi-automated dispatching controls.  
* Intelligent Dispatch Heuristics: Implement and benchmark dispatch heuristics (Nearest-Available vs. Load-Aware) to assign optimal internal patrol and rescue units within park limits.  
* Staff Mobile Application: Build an operational mobile client for rescue and security staff to receive high-priority dispatch alarms, follow navigation avoiding reported congestion, update operational statuses (Accepted, En Route, On Scene, Resolved), and submit digital incident closure reports with visual evidence.  
* Back-Office Administration: Implement management interfaces for guard posts, emergency assets (patrol units, mini fire engines), role-based access control (RBAC), and automated escalation rules for unacknowledged critical emergencies.  
* Empirical & Scientific Assessment: Quantify the accuracy/F1-score and Cohen’s Kappa agreement of the VLM against human ground truth, while evaluating response-time reduction and operator dispatch decision speed compared to manual baselines.

## **4\. Problem Statement** {#4.-problem-statement}

Emergency response and traffic clearance within industrial parks currently suffer from fragmented, manual coordination, leading to delayed response times and inefficient resource deployment. When a factory emergency or vehicle collision occurs, control room operators must decipher vague verbal reports without real-time visual verification or digital situational awareness.

This operational reality generates three concrete problems:

* Inaccurate Severity Assessment & Verification Delays: Lacking objective visual data, dispatchers struggle to discern minor localized incidents from high-consequence disasters, leading to either under-response (delayed escalation for severe fires) or over-response (tying up specialized units for trivial incidents).  
* Suboptimal Unit Dispatching & Traffic Impairment: Units are assigned without algorithmic consideration of real-time spatial positioning, existing task workloads, or sudden internal bottleneck congestions caused by container freight and shift transitions.  
* Absence of End-to-End Operational Traceability: Field response statuses, route milestones, and scene resolution reports are handled via disjointed radio communications without structured audit trails, impairing managerial oversight and post-incident analysis.  
* This project resolves these challenges by delivering an integrated, GIS-enabled emergency platform supported by the Qwen2.5-VL model for automated hazard classification and 3-level severity grading, ensuring that dispatchers can rapidly verify incidents, route around congestion, and mobilize internal assets effectively.

## **5\. Significance of the Project** {#5.-significance-of-the-project}

Academic & Engineering Value:

* Demonstrates a real-world application of Vision-Language Models (Qwen2.5-VL) deployed for multi-label hazard detection and ordinal severity scoring (Levels 0–3) on industrial scene imagery.  
* Provides empirical benchmarks comparing dispatch heuristics (Nearest-Available vs. Load-Aware) under simulated high-incident campus workloads.  
* Evaluates the quantifiable latency benefits of Human-in-the-Loop AI decision support against traditional manual dispatching.

Practical & Operational Value:

* Shortened Dispatch Latency: Pre-filtered reports and AI-scored queues significantly decrease the time required for operators to verify incidents and dispatch units.  
* Optimized Asset Utilization: Matches internal patrol teams and mini fire engines to emergencies based on real-time proximity, equipment capability, and current operational workload.  
* Congestion Mitigation: Allows citizens to crowdsource internal traffic bottleneck reports, enabling dispatchers and responders to reroute around gridlocks during peak manufacturing hours.  
* Traceability & Safety Governance: Offers park administrators an auditable event lifecycle with automated escalation rules to prevent unhandled Level 3 emergencies.

## **6\. Project Scope & Limitations** {#6.-project-scope-&-limitations}

In Scope

* Target Environment: Confined, closed-campus operational boundaries of High-Tech Parks (HTP).  
* Supported Incident Categories:  
* Core Emergencies: Fires (workshop fires, electrical short circuits) and Accidents (internal transport collisions).  
* Auxiliary Utility: Internal traffic congestion / bottleneck reporting (without severity scoring).  
* AI Capabilities: Integration of Qwen2.5-VL via API to perform hazard classification (\#Fire, \#Accident, \#Traffic\_Jam) and assign severity ratings (Level 0 to Level 3 for core emergencies).  
* Core Application Ecosystem:  
* Worker / Citizen Mobile Client (One-Touch SOS, traffic reporting, responder live tracking).  
* Command Center Web Dashboard (real-time live map, priority queue, dispatch controls, congestion visualization).  
* Rescue & Security Staff Mobile Client (alarm notifications, navigation, status updates, closure reporting with photos).  
* Back-Office Administration (asset directory, escalation rules, RBAC).  
* Backend & Infrastructure: Event-driven architecture with PostgreSQL/GIS, real-time WebSocket communication, and Docker-containerized deployment.

Out of Scope & Limitations

* External & Broader Emergency Types: Does not handle municipal-level incidents outside park perimeters, nor general civil emergencies such as external crimes, natural disasters, or advanced specialized medical triage beyond internal first response.  
* Municipal Infrastructure Integration: Excludes direct hardware-level integration with municipal 114/115 dispatch systems, municipal traffic light controllers, or vehicle-mounted IoT telemetry hardware.  
* Human-in-the-Loop Constraint: The platform provides decision support and semi-automated recommendations; it does not autonomously dispatch rescue units without human operator verification and confirmation.  
* Evaluation & Dataset Boundaries: The AI model is integrated via API and evaluated against a benchmarked, project-curated test dataset of industrial hazard and congestion imagery; operational performance under extreme unseen weather or severe optical distortions remains bounded by the test data distribution.  
* Commercial / Payment Gateways: Private rescue billing, fee processing, or commercial invoicing workflows are excluded.

# **II. Project Management Plan** {#ii.-project-management-plan}

## **1\. Overview** {#1.-overview-1}

### **1.1 Scope & Estimation** {#1.1-scope-&-estimation}

The system provides a real-time emergency coordination platform tailored for High-Tech Parks (HTP) and Industrial Parks, connecting citizens / internal workers, internal security/patrol units, and the Park Incident Command Center. The operational workflow is accelerated by an applied Vision-Language AI pipeline benchmarked across 5 candidate models (Qwen2.5-VL, SmolVLM, InternVL3, Llama-3.2-Vision, Pixtral-12B) for automated incident classification (\#Fire\_Explosion, \#Traffic\_Accident, \#Traffic\_Jam) and severity scoring (Level 1–3). The scope covers four core actor roles (Citizen / Internal Worker, Command Center Dispatcher, Rescue / Patrol Unit, and Park Safety Administrator) alongside the applied AI evaluation module.

### **1.2 Project Objectives** {#1.2-project-objectives}

Technical Objective: Build and deploy a fully functional MVP of the real-time emergency dispatch platform connecting citizens / internal workers, internal security dispatchers, and field rescue units within an industrial / high-tech park setting within the 7-week timeframe, guaranteeing event-driven latency between 1–3 seconds via WebSocket.

Research Objective: Empirically evaluate and fine-tune 5 Vision-Language Models (Qwen2.5-VL 2B/7B, SmolVLM-2.2B, InternVL3-2B, Llama-3.2-Vision-11B, and Pixtral-12B) on an emergency incident dataset. Deploy the champion model locally with cloud API fallback, validating against human ground truth to prove measurable reduction in dispatcher intake and triage time.

Engineering Standard: Deliver complete capstone deliverables (SRS, Architecture, Testing Reports, Benchmark Analysis, and Dockerized prototype) on schedule.

## **2\. Management Approach** {#2.-management-approach}

The management approach for the Emergency Dispatch System is designed to ensure strict quality control, rapid adaptability to complex real-world emergency workflows (such as real-time GPS tracking, AI-assisted incident verification, and intelligent vehicle dispatching), and seamless collaboration across team members. A tailored Agile/Scrum framework is adopted to deliver incremental, testable features while mitigating architectural risks early.

To govern the project across its three engineering tracks—the Backend API (emergency-dispatch-backend), the Web Dispatcher Portal (emergency-dispatch-frontend), and the Mobile Application (emergency-dispatch-mobile)—the team establishes practical operational guidelines:

\- Team Organization: Team members take primary ownership of specific technical subsystems (Backend, Web Portal, Mobile App) while collaborating cross-functionally during integration, testing, and reviews.

\- Task Tracking & Visibility: Sprints, user stories, and task states (To Do, In Progress, Review, Done) are managed transparently using a shared GitHub Project Board.

\- Communication Cadence: Daily standups (10–15 minutes) track progress and roadblocks, while weekly alignment sessions synchronize cross-repository API changes.

### **2.1 Project Process** {#2.1-project-process}

#### ***2.1.1 Process Model: 4-Sprint Agile / Scrum*** {#2.1.1-process-model:-4-sprint-agile-/-scrum}

The project implementation spans 8 weeks and is organized into four consecutive 2-week Sprints. This iterative approach ensures that functional increments are delivered and verified across all three repositories at the end of each sprint.

![][image2]

***Figure 1 \- Agile Framework*** 

#### ***2.1.2 Sprint Roadmap across the 3 Repositories*** {#2.1.2-sprint-roadmap-across-the-3-repositories}

**1\. Sprint 1 (Weeks 1 \- 2): Architecture Baseline, Authentication & Medical Profiles**

   Backend: Clean Architecture scaffolding, PostgreSQL (Neon Cloud) setup, JWT authentication, user profile with native array columns for Medical ID (chronicConditions, allergies), and ICE Contacts CRUD.

   Web & Mobile: Initialize React 19 \+ Vite and React Native Expo projects; baseline navigation and Leaflet map setup.

   API Alignment: Define and align core DTOs and REST endpoints via Swagger/OpenAPI before parallel UI implementation.

**2\. Sprint 2 (Weeks 3 \- 4): Emergency Incident Intake, Traffic Jam Reporting & Multimodal AI Classification**

   Backend: Incident intake pipeline (POST /api/incidents), media uploads, auxiliary traffic jam reporting (\#Traffic\_Jam), and Vision-Language AI hazard/severity scoring with fallback logic.

   AI Research Track: Dataset curation, annotation pipeline, and LoRA fine-tuning setup for the 5 candidate VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL, SmolVLM, InternVL3, Llama-3.2-Vision, Pixtral-12B).

   Web: Dispatcher queue view and audio-visual alerts for incoming emergency reports.

   Mobile: SOS one-touch trigger with real-time GPS coordinates (expo-location), scene photo capture (expo-image-picker), and traffic congestion reporting.

**3\. Sprint 3 (Weeks 5 \- 6): Fleet Management & Leaflet GIS Spatial Routing**

   Backend: Rescue Stations / Guard Posts and Fleet Units CRUD, OpenRouteService (ORS) matrix optimal vehicle dispatching.

   Web: Leaflet GIS interactive map displaying guard post markers, fleet tracking, incident heatmaps, and traffic congestion hotspot overlays (leaflet.heat).

   Mobile: Rescue team field interface to receive assignments and view incident navigation routes avoiding congested zones.

**4\. Sprint 4 (Weeks 7 \- 8): Incident Lifecycle, Vehicle Recall & Final Integration**

   Backend: Guest / Citizen / Internal Worker SOS self-cancellation with automated vehicle recall (Recall to Base), emergency contact SMS dispatch payload generation.

   AI Deployment: Benchmark analysis of 5 VLMs, containerized local hosting of the selected Champion model (FastAPI / vLLM), and cloud fallback (OpenRouter API).

   Cross-Platform: End-to-end integration testing across Mobile, Web, and Backend; bug fixing and performance tuning.

   Deployment & Delivery: Cloud deployment on Neon DB and Docker hosting, final acceptance testing, and project presentation preparation.

#### ***2.1.3 Definition of Ready (DoR) and Definition of Done (DoD)*** {#2.1.3-definition-of-ready-(dor)-and-definition-of-done-(dod)}

**1\. Definition of Ready (DoR):** 

A backlog item is ready for sprint intake when its user requirements, database schema impact, and API DTO contracts are fully specified and agreed upon.

**2\. Definition of Done (DoD): A user story is marked "Done" only when:**

 Code is peer-reviewed and merged via GitHub Pull Request without merge conflicts.

 Backend APIs are verified directly via Swagger UI and integration test runs.

 Feature workflows are verified end-to-end on both Web and Mobile by a peer team member.

### **2.2 Quality Management** {#2.2-quality-management}

Quality management focuses on structured, practical techniques that ensure system reliability in emergency scenarios without introducing corporate overhead.

#### ***2.2.1 Defect Prevention*** {#2.2.1-defect-prevention}

API Contract Alignment: Agreeing on request/response DTOs via Swagger UI before client development prevents schema mismatches between ASP.NET Core, React Web, and React Native.

Clean Architecture Boundaries: Isolating Domain entities from database and third-party API dependencies ensures that infrastructure changes do not break core dispatch logic.

Strict Data Validation: FluentValidation validates incoming payloads at the API boundary, rejecting out-of-range GPS coordinates or malformed emergency requests before reaching service layers.

TypeScript Type Safety: Strict TypeScript models shared across Web and Mobile catch data mapping and property name errors at compile time.

#### ***2.2.2 Reviewing*** {#2.2.2-reviewing}

GitFlow Branching Strategy: Development occurs on feature/\* branches merging into develop, keeping the main branch stable.

Peer Code Reviews: Every Pull Request requires at least one peer approval before merging. Reviews evaluate:

  Proper asynchronous programming patterns (async/await).

  Graceful error handling (e.g., preventing client crashes when the network is unstable).

  Clean separation of concerns and adherence to coding guidelines.

#### ***2.2.3 Unit & Component Testing*** {#2.2.3-unit-&-component-testing}

Backend Testing: xUnit test suites targeting critical business rules in EmergencyDispatch.Application:

 Incident cancellation logic: Verifying incidents can be cancelled during pending/dispatched stages with automatic rescue vehicle recall, but blocking cancellation once completed.

Medical ID array processing and primary ICE contact assignment integrity.

Client Component Verification: Testing UI components on Web and Mobile to ensure proper rendering of loading spinners, form validation messages, and map markers.

#### ***2.2.4 Integration Testing*** {#2.2.4-integration-testing}

API Integration via Swagger UI & Interactive Test Lab: Systematic testing of API endpoints covering:

  Authentication flows (JWT token generation, role verification).

  Anonymous Guest SOS submission without tokens (\[AllowAnonymous\]).

  Profile and Medical ID updates with proper Vietnamese UTF-8 character encoding.

Database Mapping Verification: Testing Entity Framework Core migrations on PostgreSQL to ensure native array columns (text\[\] for chronic conditions and allergies) persist accurately.

#### ***2.2.5 System Testing*** {#2.2.5-system-testing}

Cross-Platform End-to-End Testing: Validating complete emergency workflows within the industrial park:

  Citizen / Internal Worker SOS Flow: A reporter triggers an SOS on the Mobile App → Backend logs the report, attaches Medical ID/ICE contacts, and generates SMS payload → Web Dispatcher sees incident marker on Leaflet map → Dispatcher assigns a rescue unit → Mobile receives dispatch update.

  Self-Cancellation Flow: The reporter cancels the incident before arrival → Status changes to Cancelled → Assigned rescue vehicle is automatically released back to Available (Recall to Base).

  Traffic Jam Alert Flow: A worker uploads a traffic congestion report → Hotspot displays on Dispatcher map → Rescue units receive rerouted navigation avoiding blocked entry gates.

  Interactive UI Test Lab (UItest): A custom web-based test simulator used by the team to validate all API capabilities, guest cancellations, and Medical ID features directly in the browser during development.

#### ***2.2.6 AI Model Quality & Fallback Policy*** {#2.2.6-ai-model-quality-&-fallback-policy}

Given the critical nature of emergency classification, the Multimodal AI module undergoes rigorous verification:

Empirical Benchmark Evaluation: 5 candidate fine-tuned Vision-Language Models (Qwen2.5-VL 2B/7B, SmolVLM-2.2B, InternVL3-2B, Llama-3.2-Vision-11B, and Pixtral-12B) are evaluated against an annotated test set across Fire & Explosion, Traffic Accident, and Traffic Jam detection. The champion model is selected based on macro F1-score (target ≥ 90%), latency under 3.5 seconds, and memory footprint.

Resilience & Fallback Policy: If local AI inference latency exceeds 3.5 seconds or encounters connection timeouts, the backend automatically fails over to the cloud multimodal API (Qwen2.5-VL via OpenRouter). If cloud fallback also fails, the incident is flagged for immediate manual triage (Level 0 / Unverified queue) under a strict Human-in-the-Loop policy.

## **6\. Configuration Management** {#6.-configuration-management}

### **6.1 Document Management** {#6.1-document-management}

ll project documents (SRS, SDD, meeting minutes, reports, diagrams) are managed on Google Docs/Sheets/Slides, organized into a shared Google Drive folder structure grouped by report phase (Report 1-3) and by document type (Requirements, Design, Testing, Management). Each document follows a standardized naming convention: \<ReportNo\>\_\<DocumentName\> (e.g., Report2\_Project\_Management\_Plan).

Because documents are authored directly in Google Docs, version control is handled through Google Docs built-in Version History (File \> Version history), which automatically tracks every edit and allows the team to name and restore milestone versions. This is supplemented by a manual Record of Changes table at the beginning of each document, logging the date, change type (Added/Modified/Deleted), person in charge, and a brief change description, so reviewers can see what changed without digging through the full version history. At major milestones (e.g., submitted for review, approved by supervisor), the document is exported as PDF and archived in a dedicated Submitted/ subfolder to preserve an immutable snapshot. Access is restricted to project team members and the supervisor via Google Drive sharing permissions, with commenting enabled for the supervisor to provide feedback directly in-document.

### **6.2 Source Code Management** {#6.2-source-code-management}

Source code is managed using Git, hosted on GitHub, with a shared team repository. The team follows a simplified Git Flow branching strategy:

main \- stable, production-ready code only, protected from direct pushes.

develop \- integration branch for completed features before release.

feature/\<feature-name\> \- individual feature branches created from develop (e.g., feature/ai-hazard-classification, feature/live-map-dashboard).

All changes are merged via Pull Requests, requiring at least one team member's review and approval before merging into develop, to catch integration issues early and maintain code quality. Commit messages follow a consistent convention (\<type\>: \<short description\>, e.g., feat: add severity score display on live map) to keep the commit history traceable. GitHub Issues and Projects (Kanban board) are used to track tasks, link commits/PRs to specific work items, and monitor sprint progress.

# **III. Software Requirement Specification** {#iii.-software-requirement-specification}

## **1\. Product Overview** {#1.-product-overview}

This project develops a real-time urban emergency response and dispatch management system, allowing citizens to report emergency incidents (accidents, infrastructure failures, fire, etc.) through a mobile application along with on-site images or video. The core differentiator of the system is the integration of a Vision-Language model (Qwen2.5-VL) to automatically analyze incident images, generate hazard tags, assign a severity score (Level 1–3), and compute a Plausibility Score, helping dispatch operators verify incidents and make faster decisions before assigning the most suitable rescue team to the scene.

## **2\. User Requirements** {#2.-user-requirements}

### **2.1 Actors** {#2.1-actors}

*An actor is a person, an external software system, or a hardware component that interacts directly with the system to initiate or participate in use cases. The table below defines all system actors, their roles, and their interactions within the emergency response platform:*

| \# | Actor | Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Citizen  | Report emergency incidents via a mobile app. Citizens can trigger an SOS alert by holding the report button for 2 seconds, record and transmit real-time GPS location data, attach visual evidence, track the movement and estimated time of arrival (ETA) of rescue units, and receive notifications regarding the handling status. |
| 2 | Command Center Operator  | Personnel working in the dispatch room, responsible for managing verification and coordination workflows via a dashboard. Operators review the list of pending incidents, verify hazard tags and severity levels extracted by AI, coordinate resources on an interactive map, assign rescue units, and close cases once resolved. |
| 3 | Rescue Staff  | Field responders operating emergency vehicles and using a dedicated mobile app. They receive dispatch notifications, navigate to the scene using GPS routing, update operational status (assignment accepted, en route, arrive at scene), and submit incident closure reports with visual evidence. |
| 4 | System Administrator  | The system manager responsible for configuration and technical administration. Administrators configure station information, manage user accounts and role-based permissions, and establish operational rules—such as a 5-minute escalation policy for high-severity incidents. |
| 5 | Qwen2.5-VL Service | An external multimodal AI service (combining computer vision and language capabilities) integrated into the system. This service automatically analyzes uploaded images or videos of incidents to detect types of hazards (e.g., \#Fire, \#Accident) and assign an initial severity level (Levels 1–3), thereby assisting operators with rapid verification. |

### **2.2 Use Cases** {#2.2-use-cases}

#### ***2.2.2 Descriptions***

| ID | Use Case | Actors | Use Case Description |
| :---: | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| UC-01 | Log In | Citizen | Allows users to authenticate their credentials to access protected system features and role-specific portals. |
| UC-02 | Log Out | Authenticated Users | Ends the current session and invalidates the user's authentication tokens. |
| UC-03 | Change Password | Authenticated Users | Allows authenticated users to securely update their account password. |
| UC-04 | Send SOS Emergency Report | Citizen |  Allows citizens to trigger a rapid emergency alert, including current GPS coordinates, multimedia evidence, and incident details (optional) |
| UC-05 | Capture GPS Location | System (Included in UC04) | System (Included in UC04) \| Automatically retrieves real-time latitude and longitude coordinates from the citizen's mobile device when an SOS request is sent. |
| UC-06 | Capture Multimedia Data | Citizen | Activates the device's camera or file picker to capture photos or short videos at the incident scene and attach them to the report. |
| UC-07 | Add Text Notes | Citizen | Provides an optional input field for citizens to add comments or context to the emergency dispatch request. |
| UC-08 | Track Dispatched Unit in Real-Time | Citizen | Displays a dynamic GIS map, allowing citizens to track the real-time location, route, and estimated time of arrival (ETA) of the responding unit. |
| UC-09 | Manage Emergency Profile | Citizen | Allows citizens to store and update critical personal safety data (such as blood type, medical conditions, and emergency contact numbers). |
| UC-10 | View Emergency Notifications | Citizen | Displays a real-time list of push notifications regarding report verification, vehicle dispatch, and resolution progress |
| UC-11 | View Incident History | Citizen | Allows citizens to review previously submitted SOS reports from their profiles, along with outcome summaries and timelines |
| UC-12 | Live Fleet Map Monitoring | Command Center Operator | Displays an interactive live command map showing ongoing incidents, rescue stations, and vehicle locations categorized by operational status. |
| UC-13 | View Incident Queue & Verification | Command Center Operator  | Displays newly received emergency reports—complete with hazard warnings and AI-predicted severity levels—for operator verification and priority classification. |
| UC-14 | Dispatch Rescue Units | Command Center Operator  | Allows operators to assign the most suitable and nearest rescue unit to a verified incident, either manually or via automated recommendations. |
| UC-15 | Configure Escalation Rule | System Administrator | Sets rule criteria and time thresholds (e.g., escalating Level 3 incidents if not acknowledged within 5 minutes). |
| UC-16 | User Account & RBAC Management | System Administrator | Manages user accounts, station assignments, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) authorization policies across the organization. |
| UC-17 | Incident Verification | Qwen2.5-VL Service | Evaluates submitted incident multimedia data using a Vision-Language Model to extract visual-semantic features and assist in priority classification. |
| UC-18 | Incident Severity Assessment | Qwen2.5-VL Service | Automatically assigns risk classification labels and calculates a standardized severity score (Levels 1–3) based on multimedia data analysis. |
| UC-19 | Mission Management | Rescue Staff | Oversees the entire execution process of assigned rescue missions, from request receipt to departure from the incident scene |
| UC-20 | Navigation to Incident Scene | Rescue Staff | Provides turn-by-turn directions to guide rescue vehicles directly to the incident's GPS coordinates. |
| UC-21 | Mission Status Update | Rescue Staff | Sends real-time operational status updates (Received, En route, Arrived at scene, Completed) to the Command Center. |
| UC-22 | Digital Mission Completion Report | Rescue Staff | Finalizes the mission by uploading evidentiary photos from the scene and confirming handover |
| UC-23 | Work Schedule Management | Rescue Staff | Allows rescue personnel to view duty schedules and update their availability status for shifts. |
| UC-24  | Report Traffic Congestion  | Citizen | Allows internal workers or citizens to submit localized traffic congestion reports within the park, automatically capturing GPS coordinates, attaching on-site media, and providing optional notes (without severity scoring).  |
| UC-25  | Monitor & Manage Traffic Congestion Hotspots  | Command Center Operator  | Displays active traffic congestion markers on the real-time Live Map, allowing dispatch operators to inspect report details, verify status, adjust affected radii, and dismiss or resolve bottlenecks once traffic clears.  |
| UC-26 | Congestion-Aware Navigation  | Rescue Staff  | Enables field rescue teams to receive dynamic route guidance that avoids active internal traffic congestion bottlenecks during emergency transit.  |
| UC-27  | Manage Guard Posts & Rescue Stations  | System Administrator  | Provides management capabilities for internal guard posts, patrol stations, and mini-fire stations (e.g., location coordinates, station naming, coverage zones, and operational statuses).  |
| UC-28  | Manage Rescue Equipment Inventory  | System Administrator  | Manages the centralized inventory of specialized rescue and firefighting equipment assigned to stations or guard posts (e.g., equipment type, available quantity, maintenance schedule, and operational condition).  |

#### ***3.1.2 Screen Descriptions***

| \# | Feature | Screen | Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | User Authentication | Login Screen  | Authenticates citizens via email/password or Google OAuth; supports role-switch testing and links to Registration and Password Recovery flows. |
| 2 | Account Registration | Register Screen  | Captures citizen details (Full Name, Phone Number, Email, Password) and triggers a 6-digit email verification OTP. |
| 3 | OTP Verification | OTP Verification Screen  | Validates the 6-digit OTP code with countdown timers for email verification and password reset workflows. |
| 4 | Password Recovery | Forgot Password Screen  | Initiates password reset requests via registered email, verifies identity with OTP, and securely sets a new password. |
| 5 | Instant SOS Emergency Alert | Home / SOS Screen  | The primary citizen screen: displays real-time GPS coordinates and address, a pulsing SOS button (press and hold 2s to trigger emergency camera/broadcast), and a quick hazard grid (Traffic accident, Fire, Traffic Jam…) |
| 6 | Multimedia Scene Reporting | Media Report Modal  | Pop-up interface allowing users to capture live camera photos, record videos, select library media, and append textual notes before transmitting to CAD 114/115 dispatchers. |
| 7 | Real-time Incident Acknowledgment | SOS Success Modal  | Confirms incident submission, displays the assigned Incident ID and live status, and allows the citizen to cancel false alarms. |
| 8 | Geospatial Safety & POIs | Safety Map Screen  | Interactive Mapbox map rendering user location, nearby emergency POIs (Hospitals, Fire Stations, Disaster Shelters), and active public incidents. |
| 9 | Incident History & Tracking | My Reports Screen  | Lists all past and active incidents reported by the citizen, showcasing status tags (Pending, Verified, Dispatched, Resolved, Cancelled) and AI classification severity scores. |
| 10 | Emergency Medical Profile & ICE | Profile Screen  | Manages citizen identity, blood group, medical history, drug allergies, In-Case-of-Emergency (ICE) family contacts, and automated SMS alerting preferences. |
| 11 | Quick Medical Responder Card | Medical ID Card Modal  | High-contrast emergency modal displaying vital health metrics, allergies, and emergency phone numbers for first responders at the scene. |
| 12 | Profile Editing & Configuration | Profile Edit Modal  | Multi-tab editing modal for updating: (1) Personal Identification (National ID/CCCD, DOB), (2) Medical history, and (3) ICE contact numbers. |

#### ***3.1.2.1 Recuse Staff \- Mobile Screen*** {#3.1.2.1-recuse-staff---mobile-screen}

| No | Feature | Screen | Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | Staff Authentication | Login screen | This screen is used for rescue personnel (doctors, paramedics, ambulance drivers) to authenticate into the Rescue Staff Mobile Application. The login screen includes: Input fields for staff email/username and password. "Đăng nhập" (Sign In) primary button. "Quên mật khẩu?" (Forgot Password) recovery link. Biometric authentication shortcut (Face ID / Fingerprint) for rapid emergency access. |
| **2** | Shift Operations | Staff Dashboard screen | This screen is the main operational screen of the Rescue Staff application (Kíp Trực 115). It allows on-duty crews to monitor operational readiness, assigned vehicles, and intercept incoming dispatch orders. Screen layout includes: Top profile header displaying personnel name, staff ID, assigned ambulance license plate (51A-999.99), and active shift status (*Online / Busy / Offline*). Priority Code Red dispatch alert banner with interactive trigger. Shift metrics scorecard displaying completed missions, total travel distance (km), and average ETA. Station mini-map card showing home base address, location coordinates, and vehicle status. Recently completed emergency missions list with status pills. Sticky bottom quick action dock containing shortcuts for medical supplies check, 115 SOS direct call, and shift history logs. Bottom navigation bar allowing staff to switch between the 4 main sections (*Kíp Trực, Bản Đồ Tác Chiến, Ca Cứu Hộ, Hồ Sơ Kíp Trực*). |
| **3** | Emergency Dispatch | Emergency Alert modal | This screen is a full-screen priority alert modal triggered automatically when central dispatch broadcasts an emergency mission to the response crew. Screen layout includes: A 30-second circular countdown timer ensures rapid response within the golden hour. Severity priority indicator badge (*Code Red / Critical*). Incident breakdown card detailing accident category, estimated victim count, and potential on-scene hazards. Location details including street address, distance (km), and estimated time of arrival (ETA). Two primary action buttons: "Tiếp nhận nhiệm vụ" (Accept Mission) to confirm assignment and "Từ chối" (Decline Mission) to reject with reason. |
| **4** | Field Rescue Action | Incident Overview screen | This screen is the tactical mission execution screen (Ca Cứu Hộ). It guides field rescue personnel through the standardized 4-stage rescue lifecycle. Screen layout includes: Top navigation header displaying incident reference code, severity badge, and quick dial button to 115 central dispatch. An interactive 4-stage mission stepper: *Accepted $\rightarrow$ En Route $\rightarrow$ On Scene $\rightarrow$ Completed*. Embedded Mapbox tactical navigation map displaying real-time turn-by-turn routing from current position to incident scene and onward to receiving hospital. AI Triage card displaying victim trauma assessment, audio call transcription analysis, and recommended receiving hospitals. Interactive swipe-to-confirm action slider (*SwipeToAction*) to advance stages (*Trượt để xuất phát, Đã tiếp cận hiện trường, Hoàn thành ca cứu hộ*). |
| **5** | Situational Awareness | Tactical Safety Map screen | This screen is the geospatial map screen (Bản Đồ Tác Chiến) providing full situational awareness of emergency infrastructure across the urban district. Screen layout includes: Full-viewport Mapbox vector map with dynamic POI markers for hospitals, fire stations, public shelters, and active emergencies. Category filter chips (*Tất cả, Bệnh viện, Trạm cứu hộ, Sự cố*) allowing rapid POI filtering. Real-time high-accuracy GPS marker indicating current ambulance location. Facility summary sheet displaying distance, address, emergency hotline, and external navigation launch button (*Google Maps / Apple Maps*). |
| **6** | Crew Administration | Staff Profile & Handover screen | This screen is used for crew profile management and formal shift handover procedures (Hồ Sơ Kíp Trực). Screen layout includes:  Personnel identification card with avatar, staff badge number, and duty status toggle. Dedicated ambulance profile card displaying vehicle model, license plate, and assigned station base. Assigned crew roster card (Doctor, Paramedic, Ambulance Driver) with direct phone call buttons. Tactical operational settings toggles: auto-siren activation on Code Red, high-precision GPS mode, and VHF radio frequency channel selector. "Bàn giao ca trực" (Shift Handover) protocol button to open vehicle handover checklist and "Đăng xuất" (Logout) button. |
| **7** | Equipment Inspection | Medical Equipment Checklist modal | This screen is a checklist modal used by crew members to inspect and verify mandatory medical gear and supplies on the ambulance. Screen layout includes: Categorized inventory checklist for AED defibrillators, oxygen cylinders, trauma splints, and emergency drug kits. Condition toggle controls for each item (*Đạt chuẩn / Thiếu hụt / Hư hỏng*). Digital inspection summary footer with inspection timestamp and crew lead signature.  "Lưu biên bản kiểm tra" (Save Inspection Report) submission button. |

#### ***3.1.2.2 Dispatcher \- Web screen*** {#3.1.2.2-dispatcher---web-screen}

| No | Feature | Screen | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Dispatcher Authentication | Login Screen | This screen authenticates Command Center Operators into the Dispatcher Web Portal. The login screen includes: Input fields for operator email and password.  "Đăng nhập" (Sign In) primary action button. "Quên mật khẩu?" (Forgot Password) recovery link that navigates to the Password Reset flow. Upon successful authentication with Role \= Operator, the system automatically redirects to the Main Dashboard (Live Map Page). |
| 2 | Command Center Navigation Shell | Main Dashboard Screen | The persistent shell layout wrapping all Dispatcher portal screens. Layout includes:  Left sidebar navigation with three primary links: Live Map, Incident Queue, and Analytics. Top navigation bar displaying the operator's name, role badge, and a Logout button. The DispatchProvider context is mounted once at this level to maintain shared state (incident queue, vehicle positions) across all nested screens without re-fetching on navigation.  A background polling engine calls GET /api/Incidents/queue every 20 seconds and a vehicle position simulation ticks every 2.5 seconds. |
| 3 | CAD Live Map & Fleet Monitoring | Live Map Page | The primary real-time command and control screen for the Dispatcher. Screen layout includes: Full-viewport Leaflet GIS map rendering three marker categories: (1) Incident markers color-coded by severity level and event type ( Fire/Explosion,  Traffic Accident, ); (2) Rescue vehicle markers color-coded by operational status (green: Available, yellow: En Route, red: On Scene); (3) Fixed rescue station markers. Automatic marker clustering when the map is zoomed out to prevent visual overload.  Map layer toggle (Street View / Satellite). Map legend panel explaining marker color semantics.  Clicking an incident marker opens the Dispatch Panel on the right. Clicking a vehicle marker opens the Vehicle Panel on the right. |
| 4 | Incident Dispatch | Dispatch Panel | A right-side contextual panel revealed when an incident marker is selected on the Live Map. Panel contents include:  Incident metadata: title, severity level badge, event type, hazard tags, AI summary, and confidence score.  Dispatch Engine Panel displaying vehicle recommendations automatically filtered by incident type (Fire → Fire Trucks; Accident → Ambulances;Traffic Jam → Traffic Control Unit  ).  Algorithm selector toggle: "Nearest-Available" (Haversine or Road Network distance) or "Load-Aware" (Cost \= 0.5×Distance \+ 0.3×StationLoad \+ 0.2×ActiveMissions). If no vehicle is found within the current radius, the system automatically expands the search radius in steps: 10 km → 15 km → 22.5 km → 30 km.  For Level 1–2 incidents: single-vehicle assignment with ETA confirmation. For Level 3 incidents: multi-vehicle selector allowing simultaneous assignment of 2–5 vehicles (combined fire and medical units). |
| 5 | Fleet Detail & Control | Vehicle Panel | A right-side contextual panel revealed when a vehicle marker is selected on the Live Map. Panel contents include:  Vehicle metadata: license plate, vehicle type, current operational status, and ETA to the assigned incident.  Current incident assignment details (if en route). "Hủy gán xe" (Cancel Assignment) action button that returns the vehicle to Available status and triggers an automatic re-dispatch search for a replacement unit. |
| 6 | Priority Incident Queue | Incident Queue Page | The real-time triage workstation screen for reviewing all pending emergency reports. Screen layout includes:  Sorted incident list applying the following priority algorithm: (1) Level 3 (Critical) and Level 0 (AI-Rejected / Unclassified) incidents share the top priority tier, ordered by FIFO within the tier; (2) Level 2 (Moderate); (3) Level 1 (Minor).  Level 0 incidents are visually distinguished with a prominent yellow warning flag banner to prevent false-negative oversight.  Each incident row displays: hazard tag badges, severity badge, submission timestamp, and reporter name.  New incidents detected during the 20-second polling cycle trigger a 2.2-second highlight flash animation on the corresponding row.  Clicking a row opens the Incident Detail Drawer. If the incident is currently locked by another operator, the row is grayed out and the dispatch action button is disabled. |
| 7 | Human-in-the-Loop Triage | Incident Detail Drawer | A right-side slide-over drawer for detailed incident review. Layout uses a two-column parallel structure:  Left column: Scene multimedia evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings submitted by the citizen).  Right column: AI Triage Analysis Block displaying event type classification, hazard tags, severity score (0–3), confidence percentage, and the AI-generated Vietnamese summary.  Reporter information section with phone number masked by default; clicking "Hiện số" (Reveal Number) unmasks the full phone number and records a PII access audit log entry. When a drawer is opened, a 2-minute Soft Concurrency Lock (LockedByOperatorId) is applied server-side; other operators see the incident as locked with the locking operator's name displayed.  Two primary action buttons: "Phê duyệt & Điều phối" (Approve & Dispatch) and "Bác bỏ (Báo động giả)" (Reject — False Alarm). |
| 8 | Incident Approval & AI Override | Approve Incident Dialog | A confirmation modal triggered from the Incident Detail Drawer when the operator selects the Approve action. Modal contents include:  Option to confirm the AI-suggested severity level or override it to a different level (0 / 1 / 2 / 3).  If overriding the AI result, the operator must enter a justification reason of at least 5 characters; this override reason is persisted to the immutable IncidentAuditTrail log.  "Xác nhận phê duyệt" (Confirm Approval) submit button.  On success: a toast notification confirms the approval; the incident status transitions to Verified; the system automatically triggers the Dispatch Engine to find and assign the nearest suitable vehicle; the drawer closes and the incident disappears from the queue.  On HTTP 409 Conflict (another operator approved simultaneously): an error toast notifies the current operator that the incident was already handled. |
| 9 | False Alarm & Spam Control | Reject Incident Dialog | A confirmation modal triggered from the Incident Detail Drawer when the operator selects the Reject action. Modal contents include:  Dropdown or radio selector for rejection reason: Prank Call / Wrong Address / Duplicate Report.  Optional free-text notes field.  Spam Blacklist toggle: option to block the reporter's phone number for a selected duration (7 days / 30 days / 1 year / Permanent) and add it to the BlockedPhoneNumberList.  "Xác nhận hủy" (Confirm Rejection) submit button.  On success: a toast notification confirms the rejection; the incident status transitions to Cancelled; the incident row is removed from the queue. |
| 10 | Operational Analytics | Analytics Page | A reporting and statistics dashboard providing operational performance insights. Screen layout includes:  Incident volume trend chart (daily / weekly).  Severity level distribution breakdown.  Average response time and dispatch-to-arrival ETA metrics. Top recurring hazard tags. Operator throughput statistics (incidents processed per shift). Note: currently rendered using mock data; live backend analytics API integration is pending. |
| 11 | Vehicle Dispatch Confirmation | Confirm Dispatch Dialog | A confirmation modal shown after the operator selects a vehicle from the Dispatch Engine Panel for Level 1–2 incidents. Displays the assigned vehicle's license plate, type, and ETA. Includes a "Confirm" button to finalize the assignment and a "Cancel" button to go back. |
| 12 | Multi-Vehicle Dispatch Confirmation | Confirm Multi-Dispatch Dialog | A confirmation modal for Level 3 incidents allowing simultaneous dispatch of 2–5 vehicles. Displays the full list of selected vehicles with types and ETAs. Includes "Confirm Dispatch" to finalize all assignments. |
| 13 | Cancel Assignment | Cancel Assignment Dialog | A confirmation modal triggered when the operator clicks "Cancel Assignment" from the Vehicle Panel. Prompts the operator to confirm the cancellation; upon confirmation, the vehicle status reverts to Available and the system initiates automatic re-dispatch search. |

#### *3.1.3 Web Module – Back-office System Admin Portal*  {#3.1.3-web-module-–-back-office-system-admin-portal}

| No | Feature | Screen | Description |
| :---: | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Visual Dispatch | Live Map Command Center screen | This screen is the central real-time GIS command map used by 115 dispatchers to monitor fleet vehicles and coordinate emergency units. Screen layout includes: • Full-screen interactive Mapbox map displaying live GPS telemetry of all active ambulances, fire engines, and SOS incident coordinates. • Multi-criteria filter panel to filter vehicles by type (Ambulance, Fire, Police), operational status (*Available, Dispatched, Maintenance*), and district. • Vehicle operational detail panel (VehiclePanel) showing crew names, current speed, and onboard equipment status. • Incident dispatch drawer (IncidentDispatchPanel) showing pending verified emergencies and AI-ranked nearest vehicle recommendations. • "Phát lệnh điều động khẩn cấp" (Broadcast Dispatch Order) confirmation button. |
| 2 | Incident Triage | Incident Queue Management screen | This screen is the triage queue interface used by 115 operators to inspect incoming citizen SOS requests, verify multimedia evidence, and approve dispatches. Screen layout includes: • Tabbed incident data table categorized by status (*Chờ duyệt, Đã duyệt, Đang xử lý, Đã đóng*). • Incident detail side drawer (IncidentDetailDrawer) displaying citizen contact info, reported coordinates, attached photos/videos, and call voice recordings. • AI Triage evaluation pane displaying auto-transcribed audio, extracted trauma tags, and confidence score. • Two primary decision action buttons: "Phê duyệt sự cố" (Approve Incident) to assign priority and "Bác bỏ (Báo động giả)" (Reject False Alarm). |
| 3 | Business Intelligence | Analytics & Performance Dashboard screen | This screen is an operational analytics dashboard providing executive visibility into response times and service level agreements (SLAs). Screen layout includes: • Key SLA scorecards displaying Average Response Time, Golden Hour Achievement Rate, Total Dispatches, and Fleet Utilization. • Hourly incident distribution chart and incident category breakdown pie chart (Traffic Accident, Cardiac Arrest, Fire). • Station performance leaderboard benchmarking response delays across satellite stations. • Date range picker and report export controls (*Export PDF / Excel*). |
| 4 | Infrastructure Management | Stations Management screen | This screen is an administrative back-office screen for managing the network of emergency ambulance stations and fire stations. Screen layout includes: • Stations inventory table listing Station Name, Station Code, Address, Hotline, and Operational Status. • Sub-panel (StationAssetsPanel) showing deployed vehicles and medical equipment assigned to the selected station. • Form drawer (StationFormDrawer) with embedded map picker to define station GPS coordinates and boundary data. • Action buttons for creating, editing, and deactivating emergency stations. |
| 5 | Fleet Management | Vehicles & Fleet Management screen | This screen is a fleet administration interface for monitoring vehicle profiles, GPS trackers, and maintenance schedules. Screen layout includes: • Fleet data table displaying License Plate, Vehicle Category, Home Station, Odometer, and Readiness Status. • Vehicle detail drawer showing hardware GPS Tracker ID, vehicle specs, and dispatch history. • Embedded equipment readiness checklist verifying onboard life-support gear. • Status dropdown selector to transition vehicles between *Available, Maintenance*, and *Out of Service*. |
| 6 | Access Control | Accounts & Permissions Matrix screen | This screen is a security management portal for administering user accounts and configuring the system-wide Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) matrix. Screen layout includes: • User accounts table listing Full Name, Email, Phone Number, System Role (*Admin, Operator, RescueStaff, Citizen*), and Account Status. • User status toggle switch to instantly activate or suspend user credentials. • Dynamic permission matrix tab (PermissionMatrix) displaying a granular grid of functional privileges mapped across user roles. • "Lưu thay đổi ma trận" (Save Matrix Changes) confirmation button. |
| 7 | Automation Policy | Escalation Rules Configuration screen | This screen is an administrative settings screen for defining automated incident escalation rules when response thresholds are breached. Screen layout includes: • List of active escalation rule cards showing trigger criteria and automated response actions. • Rule builder drawer (EscalationRuleFormDrawer) for defining priority levels, maximum response timeout (minutes), and geographical radius. • Multi-level escalation actions selector (secondary SMS dispatch, supervisor escalation, neighboring station fallback). • Master enable/disable toggle switch for each rule. |

| **3** | Scene Hazard AI Analysis | Automated AI Vision Hazard Extractor (Qwen-VL) | On SOS creation with media, the backend automatically triggers the **Qwen-VL** model to extract **\#hazardTags**, summarize emergency context in Vietnamese, and compute preliminary severity levels (**Severity 1–3**) for dispatcher queues. |
| **4** | Real-time Incident Sync | SignalR Live Dispatch Real-time Sync | Establishes a persistent WebSocket connection between the mobile app and the backend; pushes live state changes to the citizen when an incident is verified (**Verified**), rescue units are en route (**Dispatched**), or the case is resolved (**Completed**). |
| **5** | Mobile Push Alerts | Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM Push Service) | Delivers high-priority background push notifications to the victim's device when the app is minimized or locked, communicating rescue unit plate numbers and estimated arrival times (ETA). |
| **6** | Auth & Security Daemon | Automated Email OTP & Security Alert Worker | Generates cryptographically secure 6-digit OTP codes expiring in 10 minutes via SMTP Gmail, and dispatches instant security alert emails containing client IP addresses when credentials are changed. |
| **7** | Relative Notification | Emergency ICE Contact Dispatch Trigger | Resolves emergency contact numbers stored in the citizen's medical profile and prepares emergency coordinate payloads to facilitate instant SMS alerts when the SOS button is triggered. |

#### ***3.1.6 Entity Relationship Diagram***

![][image23]

***Figure 19 \- Entity Relationship Diagram*** 

**Entities Description**

| \# | Entity | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | User | Stores master account credentials and authorization profiles for all system participants, including Citizens, Command Center Operators, Rescue Personnel, and System Administrators. It maintains authentication credentials, emergency medical profiles (blood type, chronic conditions, allergies), assigned roles, and core contact attributes. |
| 2 | Notification | Represents outbound system alerts and messaging records dispatched to users, such as emergency dispatch task alerts, incident status transitions, automated escalation warnings, and vehicle arrival updates via in-app feeds and Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM). |
| 3 | Station | Represents physical emergency rescue stations or depot facilities strategically deployed across service areas. It maintains geographic coordinates, service radius boundaries, administrative contact info, and exercises operational ownership over stationed rescue units and personnel teams. |
| 4 | RescueUnit | Represents mobilized emergency response vehicles and mobile apparatuses (e.g., Ambulances, Fire Engines, Ladder Trucks, Rescue Boats). It tracks real-time GPS telemetry coordinates, active operational availability statuses (Available, Dispatched, OnScene, Returning, Maintenance), and station affiliations. *(Replaces legacy vehicles)*. |
| 5 | StationTeam | Defines a dedicated operational crew or duty squad organized within a specific rescue station. It manages shift staffing, crew naming, and maintains a direct 1-to-1 operational assignment to an active rescue vehicle or station standby duty. |
| 6 | StationTeamMember | Acts as the operational membership junction associating an individual rescue staff member (User) with a designated StationTeam. It enforces the constraint that each rescuer belongs to at most one active team while defining specific operational crew roles (e.g., Team Leader, Driver, Rescuer, Paramedic). |
| 7 | Incident | Captures the complete lifecycle of a reported emergency incident (SOS). It records geolocation coordinates, location addresses, reporter contact details, operational lifecycle status, verified severity levels (Level 0–3), responsible station boundaries, operator notes, and soft-lock concurrency controls. |
| 8 | IncidentMedia | Stores multimedia evidence (photographs and videos) submitted by reporting citizens or field personnel from the incident scene. It preserves secure cloud storage URLs (Cloudinary), MIME types, and file metadata to facilitate automated AI assessment and operator triage. |
| 9 | AiClassification | Stores automated scene risk evaluations and hazard classifications generated by the Vision-Language Model (Qwen2.5-VL). It persists predicted incident types (Fire/Explosion, Traffic Accident), confidence scores, hazard tags, summary assessments, and processing latency benchmarks. *(Replaces legacy AIAnalysisResult)*. |
| 10 | DispatchAssignment | Represents an official deployment order assigning a specific RescueUnit and its duty crew to an Incident scene. It tracks deployment lifecycle milestones (Dispatched, Accepted, EnRoute, Arrived/OnScene, Completed, Rejected), ETA, transit distance, algorithmic dispatch metadata, and rejection reasons. |
| 11 | CompletionReport | Represents the formal mission resolution and closure dossier submitted by the rescue crew upon completing on-scene operations. It records summary actions, victim assistance counts, handover entities (hospitals, police), and the list of utilized supplies and equipment (EquipmentUsed). *(Replaces legacy ClosureReport)*. |
| 12 | CompletionReportMedia | Stores post-incident evidentiary photographs and video recordings attached to a CompletionReport, verifying mission completion, scene stabilization, and handover status. |
| 13 | IncidentStatusHistory | Maintains an immutable chronological audit trail tracking all lifecycle state transitions of an Incident (e.g., Pending \-\> Verified \-\> Dispatched \-\> Completed \-\> Closed), logging the acting user, timestamps, role, and transitional remarks. |
| 14 | AssignmentStatusHistory | Maintains an immutable audit record tracking sequential status changes of an individual DispatchAssignment (Dispatched \-\> Accepted \-\> EnRoute \-\> OnScene \-\> Completed / Rejected), ensuring operational accountability and response time analytics. |
| 15 | IncidentAuditTrail | Provides high-granularity, append-only security audit logging for incident operations, recording exact before-and-after JSON state snapshots, actor IP addresses, and user-agent metadata. |
| 16 | RefreshToken | Stores cryptographically secure JWT refresh tokens used for session maintenance, token renewal, and token rotation with revocation upon password change. |
| 17 | SystemAuditLog | Logs administrative audit trails for management operations across the platform, including user role updates, station assignments, vehicle status modifications, and setting reconfigurations. |
| 18 | EscalationRule | Defines automated escalation trigger criteria, response time thresholds (daytime vs. night shift), and target notification authorities when high-severity incidents exceed acceptance SLAs. |
| 19 | EscalationLog | Records immutable audit records of automated escalation events triggered by background workers, tracking timeout durations, escalation tiers, and resolution milestones. |
| 20 | CitizenFeedback | Captures post-incident citizen feedback, satisfaction ratings (1 to 5 stars), and operational comments following emergency mission completion. |
| 21 | TrafficHotspot | Stores real-time internal traffic congestion points, obstacles, and localized bottlenecks with automated Time-To-Live (TTL: 30–45 minutes) expiration to optimize dispatch routing. |
| 22 | BlockedPhoneNumber | Maintains blacklisted phone numbers restricted from submitting emergency SOS requests due to confirmed false alarms or malicious spam reporting. |
| 23 | SystemSetting | Stores system-wide runtime operational configuration parameters, dispatch scoring weights (Nearest vs. Load-Aware), and search radius thresholds in dynamic JSON format. |

### **3.2 Citizen Mobile Features**

#### ***3.2.1 Citizen Registration*** {#3.2.1-citizen-registration}

Function trigger: Triggered by user interaction. On LoginScreen, the user taps the "Don't have an account? Register now" link to navigate to RegisterScreen.

Function description:

* Actor / Roles: Unregistered Citizen / User.  
* Purpose: Allows new citizens to create a verified personal account to access emergency response features, store personal medical profiles, and receive real-time disaster alerts.  
* Interface: Mobile Application – RegisterScreen.tsx.  
* Data processing: Collects registration inputs from citizens, performs client-side format validation, sends HTTP request POST /api/auth/register, hashes password with BCrypt, persists entities with default Citizen role, and redirects to LoginScreen upon success.

Screen layout:

![][image24]

Function Details:

a. Input Data & Validation Rules

| No. | Field Name | Data Type | Required | Validation Rules | Error Message |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Full Name | String | Yes | Minimum 2 characters, no illegal script tags | "Full name cannot be empty" |
| 2 | Phone Number | String | Yes | Valid 10-digit Vietnamese phone format (starting with 03, 05, 07, 08, 09\) | "Invalid phone number format" |
| 3 | Email | String | No | Valid RFC 5322 email format | "Invalid email format" |
| 4 | Password | String | Yes | Minimum 8 characters, containing at least 1 letter and 1 number | "Password must be at least 8 characters long" |
| 5 | Confirm Password | String | Yes | Must exactly match the Password field | "Passwords do not match" |

b. Business Rules:

* Phone Number and Email must be unique across the entire user database.  
* Newly registered accounts are automatically granted the Citizen role.

c. Scenarios:

* Normal Flow (Happy Path): Citizen enters valid data \-\> taps "Register" \-\> system registers account \-\> success toast displayed \-\> user is navigated to LoginScreen.  
* Abnormal Cases:  
  * Duplicate Phone Number: The system displays "This phone number is already registered".  
  * Network / Server Error: The system displays "Unable to connect to dispatch server, please try again later".

#### ***3.2.2 Citizen Authentication & Login*** {#3.2.2-citizen-authentication-&-login}

Function trigger: Triggered upon application startup when no valid authentication token session exists in local storage, or when the user manually logs out.

Function description:

* Actor / Roles: Registered Citizen.  
* Purpose: Authenticates citizen credentials and issues JSON Web Tokens (Access Token & Refresh Token) to secure subsequent API requests.  
* Interface: Mobile Application \- LoginScreen.tsx.  
* Data processing: Collects Phone/Email and Password, sends HTTP request POST /api/auth/login, backend verifies BCrypt password hash and user status, returns JWT Access Token, Refresh Token, and user identity profile, and client securely saves tokens into encrypted storage and directs user to CitizenNavigator.

Screen layout:

![][image25]

Function Details:

a. Input Data & Validation Rules

| No. | Field Name | Data Type | Required | Validation Rules | Error Message |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Phone / Email | String | Yes | Must not be empty | "Please enter your phone number or email" |
| 2 | Password | String | Yes | Must not be empty | "Please enter your password" |

b. Business Rules:

* More than 5 consecutive failed attempts temporarily locks login attempts for 15 minutes.  
* An HTTP interceptor automatically uses the Refresh Token to renew expired Access Tokens seamlessly.

c. Scenarios:

* Normal Flow: Citizen inputs valid credentials \-\> taps "Login" \-\> system validates \-\> user is immediately navigated to HomeScreen (Emergency SOS).  
* Abnormal Cases:  
  * Invalid Credentials: Displays "Incorrect phone/email or password".  
  * Deactivated Account: Displays "Your account has been temporarily disabled".

#### ***3.2.3 Emergency SOS Alert Trigger*** {#3.2.3-emergency-sos-alert-trigger}

Function trigger: Citizen presses and holds the circular SOS pulse button continuously for 2 seconds (Hold 2s gesture) on HomeScreen.

Function description:

* Actor / Roles: Citizen / Victim in life-threatening distress.  
* Purpose: Enables one-touch emergency distress reporting with high-precision GPS coordinates, reverse-geocoded address, and instant incident priority to the dispatch coordination center.  
* Interface: Mobile Application \- HomeScreen.tsx (SosPulseButton.tsx & SosSuccessModal.tsx).  
* Data processing: Retrieves high-accuracy GPS coordinates (accuracy ±3m) from device location hardware, performs Reverse Geocoding via Mapbox API to obtain readable street address, prompts instant camera capture of the scene (or sends immediate distress signal without media), issues POST /api/incidents with maximum priority tag, saves incident ID into local device storage (AsyncStorage), and triggers automated emergency SMS alerts containing current GPS coordinates to registered ICE contacts.

Screen layout:

![][image26]![][image27]

Function Details:

a. Input Data & Validation Rules

| No. | Field Name | Data Type | Required | Data Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Latitude / Longitude | Double | Yes | Device GPS hardware sensor |
| 2 | Location Address | String | Yes | Mapbox Reverse Geocoding API |
| 3 | Reporter Phone | String | Optional | Extracted from logged-in user profile |
| 4 | Media Snapshot | Image / URI | Optional | Live Camera capture |

b. Business Rules:

* Requires holding the button for 2,000 ms (2 seconds) to prevent false alarms caused by accidental taps.  
* Provides an immediate "Cancel Alarm" button allowing citizens to cancel the signal if triggered accidentally, sending the cancellation reason back to dispatchers.

c. Scenarios:

* Normal Flow: Citizen holds SOS button for 2 seconds \-\> camera captures scene \-\> coordinates and snapshot uploaded \-\> success dialog appears with incident tracking code (\#XXXX) and dispatcher status.  
* Abnormal Cases:  
  * Location Permission Denied: Dialog prompts users to grant device location permissions.  
  * No Internet Connectivity: The application prompts a direct phone call shortcut to national emergency hotlines (114 Fire / 115 Ambulance).

#### ***3.2.4 Hazard Incident Reporting with AI Analysis*** {#3.2.4-hazard-incident-reporting-with-ai-analysis}

Function trigger: Citizen selects one of 4 quick hazard cards on HomeScreen (Fire, Traffic\_Jam, Accident) or taps the "Quick Media Bar" (Photo, 5s Video, Note).

Function description:

* Actor / Roles: Citizen / Bystander witnessing a public safety hazard.  
* Purpose: Submits rich multimedia evidence (photo, short video, scene description) to help AI models automatically evaluate hazard severity (Level 1 to Level 3\) to assist dispatchers in resource triage.  
* Interface: Mobile Application \- MediaReportModal.tsx & QuickHazardGrid.tsx.  
* Data processing: Captures media asset via device camera or library, uploads media asset to cloud storage via mediaService, gathers real-time GPS coordinates, calls POST /api/incidents with hazard classification tags, and receives AI computer vision evaluation response (severity assessment and detected emergency elements).

Screen layout:

![][image28]![][image29]

Function Details:

a. Input Data & Validation Rules

| No. | Field Name | Data Type | Required | Validation Rules |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Hazard Category | String | Yes | Must belong to: \#Fire, \#Accident. |
| 2 | Media File | Image / Video | No | Image file \<= 10MB, video duration \<= 15 seconds |
| 3 | Description / Note | String | No | Maximum 500 characters |
| 4 | GPS Coordinates | Coordinates | Yes | Current latitude & longitude of reporter |

b. Business Rules:

* When an image is provided, backend AI models automatically analyze smoke, flames, or vehicle damage to estimate severity levels.

c. Scenarios:

* Normal Flow: Citizen taps "Fire" \-\> takes a photo of the incident \-\> types brief description \-\> taps "Submit Report" \-\> report confirmed with assigned incident ID and AI severity rating.  
* Abnormal Cases:  
  * Media Upload Failure: App notifies citizen and offers the choice to submit the report with text and location only.

#### ***3.2.5 Safety Map & Emergency POI Navigation*** {#3.2.5-safety-map-&-emergency-poi-navigation}

Function trigger: Citizen selects the second tab from the bottom navigation bar: Safety Map (SafetyMapTab).

Function description:

* Actor / Roles: All Citizens.  
* Purpose: Provides geospatial awareness by rendering user location, nearby emergency infrastructure (Hospitals, Fire Stations), and active hazard zones on an interactive map.  
* Interface: Mobile Application \- SafetyMapScreen.tsx (Powered by Mapbox Vector Maps).  
* Data processing: Loads predefined emergency POI markers, fetches ongoing public incidents via GET /api/incidents, renders categorized visual markers on the Mapbox viewport, and handles camera zoom and re-centering based on user GPS.

Screen layout:

![][image30]

Function Details:

a. Interactive Controls

| Component Name | Action Type | Functional Behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Category Filter Chips | Tap | Toggles visibility: All, Hospitals & Medical, Active Incidents, Emergency Shelters |
| Recenter GPS Button | Tap | Smoothly re-centers map camera (FlyTo) to citizen's current GPS coordinates |
| Map Marker | Tap | Pops up detailed card: Facility name, address, emergency hotline, and distance |

b. Business Rules:

* Only active and in-progress incidents are displayed; resolved (Completed) incidents are excluded from the safety map.

c. Scenarios:

* Normal Flow: Citizen opens Safety Map \-\> map centers on current location \-\> taps "Hospitals" filter \-\> taps nearest hospital marker \-\> views hotline and directions.

#### ***3.2.6 Incident Reports Tracking*** {#3.2.6-incident-reports-tracking}

Function trigger: Citizen taps the third tab: My Reports (ReportsTab), or clicks the History Clock icon on the HomeScreen header.

Function description:

* Actor / Roles: Citizen who previously submitted emergency reports or triggered SOS alerts.  
* Purpose: Enables citizens to track the real-time response status and dispatch lifecycle of their reported incidents.  
* Interface: Mobile Application \- MyReportsScreen.tsx.  
* Data processing: Retrieves incident IDs from local device storage (AsyncStorage) and user account token, calls GET /api/incidents with filtering parameters, and renders chronologically ordered incident cards with color-coded status badges.

Screen layout:

![][image31]

Function Details:

a. Displayed Card Attributes:

* Incident Code: Short hashed identifier (e.g., \#A1B2C3D4).  
* Rescue Status Badge:  
  * Pending: Incident received and awaiting triage (Grey).  
  * Verified: Confirmed by dispatcher (Blue).  
  * Dispatched / InProgress: Rescue team / Ambulance en route to scene (Orange/Amber).  
  * Completed: Rescue operation completed (Green).  
* Severity Level: Level 1 to Level 3 (Catastrophic).  
* Timestamp & Location: Reporting time and street address.

b. Business Rules:

* Supports Pull-to-Refresh gesture to poll the latest status from dispatchers.

c. Scenarios:

* Normal Flow: Citizen opens tab \-\> views list of submitted incidents \-\> monitors real-time arrival of dispatched rescue units.  
* Abnormal Cases:  
  * No Previous Reports: Displays an informative empty state illustration: "No incident reports submitted yet".
